html:
Introduction

Washington State licenses Home Care Agencies to provide non-medical personal care services. The WA State Department of Health — Office of Health Systems Oversight (OHSO) oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Washington’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Washington’s Regulations

WA DOH OHSO licenses home care agencies under WAC 246-335. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training (75-hour certification), and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the WA Secretary of State, apply for home care agency license through DOH, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Washington benchmarks: Private pay rates $26-$36/hour, Medicaid rates $20-$28/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

WA requires 75-hour home care aide certification and background checks for all caregivers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting DOH OHSO requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Seattle, Spokane, Tacoma, and statewide.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What training is required? Washington requires 75 hours of training for home care aide certification.
